title: Movie files and the wait before the opening movie

title: Autosave notice and the save icon
summary: No dedicated 'this game autosaves' notice text is in the menu files. The game shows a small save icon in a corner whenever it writes, drawn from 30 frames in the SB_SaveIcon sheet.

title: Loading tips text and unlock flags
summary: There are 86 tip titles and 86 tip bodies. KnowledgeLoadScreenItemParam has 85 rows that point at a tip; 77 are unlocked by an event flag (many by 6341 and 6342) so tips appear as the player meets the matching mechanic.
values: Files ローディングタイトル / ローディングテキスト ids 50 to 316 (50 Lock On to target, 53 Mikiri Counter, 123 Finisher Deathblow, 125 Unseen Aid Chance, 135 Free Combat, 153 Healing Gourd). KnowledgeLoadScreenItemParam fields unlockFlagId, invalidFlagId (all -1), msgId; row 1 msgId 51 unlock 6341. Common events 810 and 811 call Disable Loading Screen Tips 2003[76].
how: The tip pool is the rows whose unlock flag is on; the screen draws one at random. After each ending cutscene branch the event sets Disable Loading Screen Tips to 1 so the next load shows none.
check: Rest at an idol early and late in a run: the tip list should grow as flags 6341 and later turn on.
note: How the random pick is made is not traced.

title: What triggers an autosave
summary: The game saves by itself all the time. In the event scripts a Save Request runs at 32 places: after boss and mini-boss deaths, after story cutscenes and when a respawn point is set. Resting at an idol and Quit Game also save, and item pick-ups are written to the save as they happen.
values: Save Request 2000[5] call sites: common 1 (event 910 with Set Player Respawn Point 1112955), common_func 5 (20006000, 20006002, 20006003, 20006004, 20006007: enemy death events), m10 3, m11_00 4, m11_01 1, m11_02 9 (for example 11120100 after the intro cutscene, 11125800 around the Reservoir boss), m13 1, m15 3, m20 2 (plus 2 in the 12_60 copy), m25 1.
how: Save Request tells FrpgSaveLoadMan to write the profile. Idols, Quit Game and pick-ups save through the menu and item code, not EMEVD.
check: Kill a mini-boss and watch for the save icon at its death.
note: The idol, item and quit triggers are community only.

title: Quit Game from the pause menu
summary: Options in the pause menu has Quit Game. It asks to save and return to the title menu, and writing the save there is what keeps the latest progress. Closing the window instead can lose the newest progress and shows a warning on the next start.
values: Texts 115002 and 110500 Quit Game; dialog 110500 'This will save the game and return to the Title menu. Are you sure?', 110501 'Quit game and return to title menu?'; 400003 warning shown when the game last ended without Quit Game; help 110500 'Save the game and return to the Title Menu.' Exe Check_ReturnTitle, RegistReturnTitle, OnReturnTitle.
how: Quit Game runs the save, then the return-to-title step.

ours.where: src/game_menu.rs (Options list has Return to Title and Quit Game; no save to write)

check: Choose Quit Game, then Continue: you should stand where you quit.

title: Where a reload puts you
summary: After Quit Game the web guides say you resume where you quit. After a crash or after dying the game puts you at the last rested idol (or an event respawn point). The data holds the respawn rule; the quit position is not shown in the data.
values: Set Player Respawn Point 2003[23] 19 uses (map.respawn-checkpoint); SaveDataStartPointInfo in the save; web: Quit Game acts as a quick save, forced close restarts at the nearest idol without refilling.
how: StartPointInfo holds the position written by Quit Game; the respawn point is the idol.

needs.why: the idol and event respawn rule

check: Quit Game away from an idol, then Continue; then kill the game process, Continue again and compare spots.
note: The StartPointInfo link is inferred from the class name.

title: Three endings in the Reservoir event
summary: Event 11120110 in map m11_02 handles the other endings. After the final boss flag 9312 and Wolf alive, it reads three choice flags (11125707, 11125708, 11125709) and plays one branch. Each branch sets its own ending flag (6830, 6831, 6832) and an achievement (9, 10, 11).
values: Branch A: scene 11020110, flags 20 and 6830, achievement 9. Branch B: scenes 11020120 then 11020121, flags 21 and 6831, achievement 10. Branch C: scene 11020100, flags 22 and 6832, achievement 11. All branches set 6900 off, 6901 on. Setters of 11125707 to 11125709 are not in the EMEVD files.
how: The choice flags are set by the last talk (ESD) before the fight.

title: Ending cutscene sequence pattern
summary: Every ending branch follows one script: fade the menu out in 0.5 s, put the player in the ending SpEffect 4702 and make him immortal, swap the map parts for the ending set, fade in, play the cutscene with its lighting, wait for it, then restore and set flags.
values: Calls: Set Menu Fade 2003[82] (1, 0.5 s); SpEffect 4702 on 10000; Set Character Immortality 1; Force Animation Playback map animation 8901000 id 51 then 1; Activate Map Part 8907050 on and 8907000 to 8907100 off; Set Area Gparam Sub ID (11, 2); Menu Fade 0; Play Cutscene and Warp Player With Lighting 2002[13] (cutscene, play mode 16, warp point 1122800, area 11 block 2, player 10000, time of day 5 or 1); IF Ongoing Cutscene Finished; Set 9530; clear 4702; immortality 0.
how: The castle branch uses the same pattern with warp point 1112812, block 1 and time of day 3.
check: Play to an ending and watch the fade before the scene.

title: Rewards after any ending
summary: Common event 295 waits for any ending flag (6830, 6831, 6832 or 6833), then 3 s later gives an armor piece (lot 5710, id 400000) and Another's Memory: Ashina (lot 5740, goods 9810) when the Sculptor flag 8306 is off.
values: Event 295: skip if goods 9810 owned; IF flag 6830 or 6831 or 6832 or 6833; IF 8306 off; wait 3.0 s; Award Item Lot 5710; Award Item Lot 5740.
how: Memory 9810 lets Wolf change appearance at an idol.
check: After any ending, rest at an idol and open Change Form.
note: The armor name for id 400000 was not looked up.

title: Credits roll movie
summary: The credits are the staff list movie stafflistmovie.bk2 (598104408 bytes, Bink 2), started by the exe ending step. The data has no length, and whether the player can skip is not recorded.
values: File stafflistmovie.bk2; enum Movie_StaffRoll; classes EndingStep, GamesComEndingStep, E3EndingStep; flag bRequestToEnding; the movie subtitle file has no credits lines. Slots Movie_EndingBad and Movie_EndingGood exist but no files ship.
how: EndingStep requests the movie, plays it, then calls the return flow. No EMEVD instruction starts a movie.
check: Time the credits on a recording and hold a button to see if it skips.
note: Needs a recording for length and skip.

title: After the credits: NG+ prompt
summary: When the credits end the game asks whether to start playthrough N+1 now. If the player says no, the game returns to play and the same offer stays at the large Sculptor's Idol in the Dilapidated Temple. Saying yes starts the next cycle.
values: Dialog 450000 'Start playthrough #<?nextLoopCount?> now?' (adds: later via the large Sculptor's Idol in the Dilapidated Temple) and 450001 warns that the current playthrough cannot be returned to. The dialog is built in exe function FUN_1411d9a10. Cycle count lives at GameDataMan +0x70.
how: A menu job builds the two-line confirm; on yes it increments the cycle and reloads.
check: Finish an ending and watch for the prompt after the credits.
note: The 'Journey onward' wording from the task is not in the English text; the wording is playthrough #N.

title: What the new cycle resets and keeps
summary: When a new cycle starts, common event 50 strips about 70 goods from the player (including the Bell Demon 3730 to 3733 and Kuro's Charm 9003), forces the starting armor, clears the Charmless flag 6911, flag 6901 and 9530, and restarts the world events. Skills, gourd, prosthetics and levels are kept.
values: Event 50 when 6901 is on and 11120100 is off: Remove Item From Player for 0:5700, 0:7300, 0:680000 and 3:2000, 2300, 2310, 2930, 2400, 2500 to 2503, 3730 to 3733, 3990, 9000 to 9012, 9020, 9052, 9070 to 9091, 9181 to 9228, 9400 to 9405, 9500 to 9516, 9560, 12600 to 12620; Force Player Armor Equip (1, 141000) and (2, 112000); then IF Game Cycle 3[17]; Set Flag 6910 If Game Completed On Any Save; 6911 off; 6901 off; 9530 off; clear SpEffect 400; remove 3 of goods 500.
how: Web: items, skills, levels and gourd carry; NPC and world state reset; the Bell Demon does not carry; Kuro's Charm is given again after a completed game (event 11120120 awards lot 3300 = goods 9003 when 6910 is on).

needs.why: the bell is removed at cycle start

check: Finish with the Bell Demon and Kuro's Charm owned, start NG+, open the key item list.
note: Which goods ids are key items was not looked up for each of the removed ids.

title: Game clear and ending flags
summary: A small set of flags tracks clears: 6900 and 6901 flip after each major ending, 6830 to 6833 mark which ending was seen, 6910 is set from any save with a cleared game, 6911 is Charmless mode, and 6912 to 6919 count Charmless clears.
values: 6900=0 and 6901=1 set in m11_01 11110100 and m11_02 11120110 branches. 6830/6831/6832 (Reservoir branches), 6833 (castle). 6910 set by 2003[86] Set Flag 6910 If Game Completed On Any Save (common event 50). 6911 read by event 800 (applies SpEffect 8610 when on) and by the area scaling events; at the ending when 6911 is on the first unset flag of 6912 to 6919 is set (11110100 and 11120110 tails). CharaInitParam row 10160 Game clear.
how: EMEVD tests the flags; the exe writes the cycle count; the achievements come with the same events.
check: Read flags 6830 to 6833 and 6910 to 6919 with memscope after finishing.
note: The meaning of 6900 and 6901 is read from where they are set, not from a name.

title: Achievement awards in the scripts
summary: Event scripts call Award Achievement at 26 places with ids 1, 2, 9 to 13, 16, 17 and 19 to 33. Most are boss defeats, four are endings and one is the first resurrection. The web list has 34 trophies, so the other ids come from the exe or from talk scripts.
how: 2003[28] Award Achievement forwards the id to Steam through SteamUserStats (exe).
check: Open the Steam achievement page and compare ids 1 and 19 with the first resurrection and 17 bosses.
note: The name for each id was not tied here; only 1, 9 to 12 and 19 are matched by context. Total ids are 26 call sites over 25 ids.

title: Banner texts: DEATH, SHINOBI EXECUTION and others
summary: The big center banners are event texts: SHINOBI EXECUTION, SCULPTOR'S IDOL FOUND, DEATH, IMMORTALITY SEVERED, then GRACIOUS GIFT OF TEARS, SINISTER BURDEN, BURDEN DISPELLED, UNSEEN AID, DRAGONROT HEALED and INNER REFLECTION CONQUERED. DEATH is drawn with the brush kanji 死.
values: イベントテキスト 10010900 SHINOBI EXECUTION, 10010901 SCULPTOR'S IDOL FOUND, 10010902 DEATH, 10010903 IMMORTALITY SEVERED, 10010950 to 10010955; sprites MENU_Death and MENU_Death_02 (extracted/hud); MenuParam SoloPlayDeath_ToFadeOutTime 2.5 s (Paramdex: seconds after the death banner shows before the fade out starts).
how: Display Banner 2007[2] shows an event text by id; the death banner is raised by the player death code.
check: Die once: DEATH shows and the screen fades about 2.5 s later.

title: Resurrect or Die prompt
summary: When Wolf has a node left the death screen offers two choices with key icons: Resurrect and Die. If he takes no node, or gives up, the death is final and the game reloads at the checkpoint.
values: Event text 10010390 '<?kgiconKc@16?>: Resurrect' (attack key), 10010391 '<?kgiconKc@18?>: Die' (guard key); delay 1.8 s and 15 s window per deathblows.true-death-flow.
how: The prompt is the action panel; the reload goes through the respawn point and a fade.

ours.where: src/menu.rs (RMB / K Die, LMB / J Resurrect)

check: Die with a node: the two prompts show at the bottom after 1.8 s.

title: Loss on death and Unseen Aid text
summary: Death halves skill experience and sen. A rare Unseen Aid spares that loss and shows the UNSEEN AID banner. The chance can be read in the pause menu. Two tutorial pages explain this, and Rot Essence items lower the chance.
values: Tutorials 10024800/10024801 'Loss upon Death' (halved, gone for good), 10024810/10024811 'Unseen Aid' (chance shown in the Pause Menu); banner 10010953 UNSEEN AID; stat label 10110 Unseen Aid; loading tip 125 'Unseen Aid Chance'; Rot Essence items 9500 to 9526 reduce the chance.
how: Unseen Aid is rolled when Wolf dies; the pages show the first time the matching flag is met.
check: Die with sen in hand and read the banner and the sen total.
